newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt tells Israel honour accords to end unrest.
newsitem.headline: Egypt tells Israel honour accords to end unrest.

text.p: Egypt told Israel the way to stop violence in the West Bank was to fulfil its agreements with the Palestinians, starting with redeployment in the town of Hebron.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak from Paris to ask him to help calm the situation after Israeli troops killed five Palestinians and injured about 300 in the Ramallah area.

"Mubarak explained to Netanyahu the urgent need to carry out agreements signed by Israel and the Palestinian Authority, as the way to stop the acts of violence and avoid a deterioration in the situation, starting with redeploying Israeli forces in the town of Hebron," government newspapers said on Thursday.

"Netanyahu promised to deal with the situation and noted that the joint Palestinian-Israeli liaison committee would meet within the next few days to agree on how to implement the Palestinian-Israeli agreements," they added, quoting Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif.

"President Mubarak has said many times that peace is the way to achieve security and stability in the region, and has many times warned of the dangers of not taking practical steps towards peace and implementing the agreements," Sherif added.

"President Mubarak believes that by proceeding to build the tunnel (under the Wailing Wall) the Israeli government is making the situation more complicated, angering the Palestinians and encouraging acts of violence," Sherif said.
"It constitutes an obstacle to the peace process, and action to deal with this must be taken without delay," he added.

The government newspaper al-Ahram reported that in Paris Netanyahu said he welcomed the idea of a meeting with Mubarak as soon as he ends his current European tour. It did not say who proposed the meeting.
